item.title: Brewers Hitters Have Eye Popping Career Numbers Against Rays Top Three Pitchers
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers shortstop Cooper Pratt The World Series starts on Friday with Jacob Misiorowski likely facing off against Drew Rasmussen in Game 1. Rasmussen, Freddy Peralta and Nick Martinez have performed well in October and have, quite frankly, been better than Misiorowski, Logan Henderson and Robert Gasser. However, they could face some problems against a pesky Brewers lineup. Here are the Brewers' current hitters' numbers against each of the Rays' top three starters in their careers: Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! Vs. Rasmussen 12-for-48 .752 OPS 3 HR 3 BB Vs. Peralta 13-for-36 1.034 OPS 2 HR 3 BB Vs. Martinez 30-for-122 .737 OPS 6 HR 4 BB Those numbers are totals for the Brewers' 13 position players for the World Series combined against each starter. However, those totals lack context. The Brewers have faced each of those pitchers once this season and the numbers are not so great. Additionally, when the Brewers faced Peralta, he was on the New York Mets and had not yet been fixed by the Rays. Against Peralta this season, the Brewers had eight hits, including three doubles and two home runs. Against Rasmussen, the Brewers had three hits, and one of those was a home run by Brice Turang. Against Martinez, the Brewers had four hits, including one double and one home run. The Rays' top three starters may not have the best numbers in their career against the 13 players they may see in the Fall Classic, but this year they have had the edge. The Brewers have never faced this version of Peralta, so that could be the most pivotal matchup of the series. More MLB: Dodgers Reveal Whether Shohei Ohtani Will Need Surgery This Offseason

item.title: Fanatics making Valkyries jerseys impossible to get during WNBA Finals
item.description: Valkyries fans cheer between the third and fourth quarters during game two of the WNBA Finals between the Golden State Valkyries and the Atlanta Dream at Chase Center in San Francisco on Oct. 19, 2026. (Douglas Zimmerman/SFGATE) The Fanatics frustrations have made their way to Golden State Valkyries fans . While the WNBA shop proudly advertises that a fan can shop for Valkyries or Dream gear during this historic WNBA Finals series between Golden State and Atlanta, those who want to get a jersey representing their Bay Area team almost certainly won't get their jersey before the end of the series. All of the adult-sized jerseys on the site operated by Fanatics, the leading merchandise partner of every major sports league (including the WNBA) in the country, have an estimated arrival date to Bay Area ZIP codes of no earlier than Oct. 30. As of Wednesday afternoon, there are 21 Valkyries basketball jerseys available for sale, with only seven available in adult sizes. Five have an estimated arrival date of Nov. 12, which would be, at best, just under two weeks after a Game 7 decider scheduled for Oct. 31. At worst, it could mean a jersey would arrive 17 days after the end of this series if it was to end in five games. The other two adult-size jerseys have an estimated arrival date of Oct. 30 and would only arrive with one game to spare in the series at best. However, those jerseys are the Fanatics-manufactured replicas, which don't have the same level of quality as the other five that are manufactured by Nike and Jordan. There is some better news for those who want to get children-sized jerseys, as six of the 14 youth-size jerseys available have an estimated arrival date of Oct. 23, just before Game 4 is scheduled to happen. Still, of the remaining eight, six also have an estimated arrival of Oct. 30, one (a Fanatics-made Juste Jocyte jersey) has an estimated arrival of Nov. 5, and a custom all-star jersey has an estimated arrival of Nov. 12. This would be frustrating, but understandable, if the circumstances with other WNBA jerseys were consistent, which isn't quite the case. A jersey for Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark, whose team was eliminated in the first round on Oct. 1, has an estimated arrival date of Oct. 28, before Game 6 is scheduled to take place and before any adult Valkyries jerseys would arrive. Where there is consistency is the issues that sports fans in the Bay Area have had to put up with regarding Fanatics. In 2024, the only Super Bowl jerseys available were the 49ers' home red ones . The only problem was that the Niners were wearing white that Super Bowl, and the company later explained that it was because it simply ran out of white jerseys throughout the season. Earlier this season, Giants fans were left to deal with a lack of inventory for their baseball jerseys . This issue came two months after Fanatics issued an apology to Seahawks and Patriots fans for, once again, failing to have enough Super Bowl jerseys for their champion

item.title: Jon Jones Admits Ilia Topuria Threatened His UFC GOAT Status Before White House Setback
item.description: The debate over the greatest UFC fighter of all time has produced plenty of contenders, but Jon Jones remains a popular choice among fans and pundits alike. His dominance inside the Octagon, spanning multiple eras and two weight divisions, gives him a strong claim to the throne. While his career has been marred by controversies outside the cage, his fighting legacy is difficult to overlook. Legends such as Anderson Silva, Georges St-Pierre, and Demetrious Johnson have all entered the GOAT conversation, with Islam Makhachev also strengthening his case in recent years. Yet, Jones continues to stand out as the benchmark for greatness . Interestingly, the former two-division champion recently revealed that Jones viewed Ilia Topuria as a potential threat to his place atop the all-time rankings. Jon Jones Remains a Fan of Ilia Topuria Despite Brutal UFC White House Loss In a recent interview with Prince St. Pizza , Jones admitted that Topuria was an exciting fighter to watch. “Ilia Topuria [excites me]. Before that White House card, I looked at him as [invincible]. As bad as I want other fighters to come and beat my records and become the next greatest, there’s another side of me that wants to hold onto that for my kid’s sake and my family’s honor.” Jones went on to explain why he saw the Spaniard as a potential threat to his GOAT status. “Honestly, I thought Ilia would be the first threat to be considered the greatest of all time, and then we saw what happened to him.” However, Topuria’s brutal loss to Justin Gaethje at the UFC White House event took a major hit on his momentum. The Spaniard was stopped at the end of the fourth round and retired on his stool, allowing Gaethje to claim the undisputed lightweight title in front of the White House. He comes from a successful family, and he’s a guy who doesn’t have to fight; he doesn’t need the money, but he does it out of love, and those are the reasons that made me a big Ilia fan.” With Jones seemingly done with his fighting career and Topuria looking to return with an immediate rematch against Gaethje, all eyes will be on how the Spaniard responds to the biggest setback of his career.

item.title: Packers Rumors: 2 Defensive Line Targets After Key Injuries
item.description: Oct 19, 2025; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Green Bay Packers defensive lineman Warren Brinson (91) against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Michael Zimmelman, Editor Early on this season, the Green Bay Packers had a serious problem in the trenches. The coaching staff entered the year trusting an offensive line built largely from homegrown talent, foolishly believing its in-house options were ready for the responsibilities that come with blocking in the NFL. Through the first three weeks, Green Bay’s starters consistently misidentified blocking assignments, which left Jordan Love under constant duress and exposed the flaws in the organization’s preseason evaluations. Green Bay Packers defensive end Dani Dennis-Sutton (51) and defensive tackle Jonathan Ford (96) pressure Chicago Bears quarterback Case Keenum on Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026, at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin. The Packers won the game, 31-7. Tork Mason/Green Bay Press-Gazette Two Defensive Line Targets After Key Injuries Packers GM Brian Gutekunst responded by bringing in three veterans , with Laken Tomlinson starting three consecutive games from Weeks 4-6 (the Packers won all of those games) and Kevin Zeitler serving as a player-coach in practice. Mekhi Becton also provides insurance on the practice squad in case of any more injuries. However, just as Green Bay has begun to stabilize one side of the trenches , injuries have created a new crisis on the defensive front. A season-ending torn Achilles for Javon Hargrave alongside injuries to Warren Brinson and Jonathan Ford have left the Packers dangerously thin along the interior defensive line. With just four healthy players available at the position, Green Bay may have to lean on rookies Chris McClellan and Anthony Campbell to keep its defense afloat. That creates a significant problem for a defense built around a base 3-4 scheme, but it could be solved by trading for or acquiring a critical veteran player. A Scheme Under Pressure The three-man front is the foundation of Jonathan Gannon’s defense . Its job is to control the line of scrimmage, absorb double teams, and keep linebackers free to attack ball carriers. Javon Hargrave provided the strength to overwhelm offensive linemen and disrupt running lanes, but his absence leaves a significant void. If McClellan and Campbell cannot hold up when starters Karl Brooks and Devonte Wyatt need a breather, opposing offenses could exploit open running lanes and limit Green Bay’s linebackers’ ability to make plays. The timing could hardly be worse, with the Packers set to face Jahmyr Gibbs, one of the NFL’s most dangerous running backs, on the road in Week 7. Gannon understands how personnel can shape a defense’s effectiveness . His Philadelphia Eagles defense improved from 10th in total defense in 2021 to second in 2022, when the team recorded a franchise-record 70 sacks and reached the Super Bowl. Several factors contributed to that turnaround, but it demonstrated the importance of having the personnel to execute his scheme. The first-year Packers defensive coordinator faces a far more difficult timeline in Green Bay than he did in Philadelphia. Without an offseason to address the weaknesses, Gannon must find solutions midseason while opposing offenses prepare to test his defense’s depleted interior. The return of Micah Parsons will undoubtedly bolster the pass rush, but the All-Pro edge rusher cannot solve the Packers’ problems at nose tackle. Defensive tackle Jordon Riley, who was injured late last season, could provide relief, but he may be another two weeks away from returning. Brinson and Ford are also expected to remain sidelined until at least Week 11. Recent addition Mazi Smith and practice squad defensive tackle David Blay Jr. offer extra depth, but the Packers may need a more reliable solution to survive a brutal stretch of games that include two divisional opponents. Two Targets to Fix the Trenches With Green Bay dangerously thin along the interior defensive line, veteran free agent Larry Ogunjobi could offer an affordable short-term solution. The 32-year-old stands 6-foot-2 and weighs 305 pounds, with 134 career games and 27.5 sacks across nine NFL seasons. Oct 20, 2024; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers defensive tackle Larry Ogunjobi (99) sacks New York Jets quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) during the first quarter at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images However, Ogunjobi’s recent production raises concerns. After serving a six-game suspension in 2025 for violating the NFL’s performance-enhancing drug policy, he recorded 19 tackles and four tackles for loss without a sack in ten games with Buffalo. He most recently tried out for the San Francisco 49ers in September but remains unsigned. His availability could make him an inexpensive midseason addition, but Green Bay would need to determine whether he can still hold his ground against double teams. Jan 11, 2026; Jacksonville, FL, USA; Buffalo Bills defensive tackle Daquan Jones (92) tackles Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence (16) during the first half in an AFC Wild Card Round game at EverBank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Melina Myers-Imagn Images Veteran defensive tackle DaQuan Jones presents a more imposing, established option. At 6-foot-4 and 320 pounds, the 34-year-old has the size and proven experience to occupy blockers and keep linebackers clean in a 3-4 scheme. Jones has played just 85 defensive snaps through six games with the New England Patriots , potentially opening the door for a larger role elsewhere. However, he remains under contract with the Patriots, which means Green Bay would need to negotiate a trade or wait for his release. Two years older than Ogunjobi, Jones carries his own age-related concerns, but his physical profile and established presence as a leader on the interior make him an intriguing target if the Packers can acquire him at a reasonable cost. The Last Word Green Bay fixed its offensive line by bringing in veterans, but the defensive front could now expose another roster-building failure. Obviously, injuries are unavoidable. However, the Packers’ run defense ranks 29th in the NFL with nine rushing touchdowns allowed, while its 44 rushing first downs surrendered are tied for fifth-most in the league. Relying on four defensive tackles to survive a grueling NFL schedule only makes matters worse. The return of Micah Parsons will be great for the pass rush, but it will not fix the lack of size and depth inside. Whether through an affordable signing like Larry Ogunjobi or a trade for DaQuan Jones, the Packers must find reinforcements before opposing offenses exploit the weakness further. Green Bay already waited too long to address their offensive line. The team cannot afford to make the same mistake twice. item.title: Enes Kanter Freedom gets luxury suite, police detail at WNBA Finals Game 3 after ‘security concerns'
item.description: Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom looks on during the second half of a game between the Chicago Sky and the Indiana Fever at Wintrust Arena in Chicago on Aug. 23. (Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom's plans to attend Game 3 of the WNBA Finals in protest of the notion of transgender participation in the league took a seating-arrangement turn on Wednesday. State Farm Arena, where Games 3 and 4 are hosted, announced in a statement that Kanter Freedom would be relocated to a private suite, citing security concerns that he brought about himself. "Enes Kanter Freedom has contacted federal, state and local authorities, the WNBA, the Atlanta Dream and State Farm Arena officials to express concerns about his personal safety during his planned attendance at Game 3 of the WNBA Finals tonight. The safety and security of our guests and team members is our highest priority," the statement read. It was not announced where Kanter Freedom originally was planning to sit at State Farm Arena, but he was sitting courtside on the baseline in an August game between the Chicago Sky and Indiana Fever. He was wearing a shirt that said: "Woman noun. an adult human female." Fever forward Sophie Cunningham had previously shared opposition to trans athletes participating in the WNBA. In August, Kanter Freedom and Sky player Natasha Cloud got into an argument during the game and he was ejected from the game as well as banned from the arena. "Following consultations with the WNBA, Dream ownership, State Farm Arena leadership and security officials, we have directed Mr. Freedom to watch tonight's game from a private luxury suite," the statement continued. "This arrangement is intended to address his security concerns and help provide a safe and positive experience for him and other guests. The suite will have additional security and will be his designated viewing location for the game. State police have also assigned an officer to Mr. Freedom at his request." Before the arena's statement, Kanter had posted a video on social media insinuating that he'd been banned from the game. "ATTENTION! Just talked to director of security of the @NBA and they are now banning us from our purchased seats. Shame on @WNBA I guess they have to escort me out of the building. Stay tuned," his post said. item.description: The Texans could see Jamal Hill again, but on enemy sidelines. Getty The Houston Texans gambled again and lost (also again), this time with Jamal Hill. “#Jaguars are signing former #Texans linebacker Jamal Hill to their practice squad now that he has cleared waivers, per a league source,” KPRC 2’s Aaron Wilson reported on X on October 21. “Hill, a former sixth-round pick and converted safety from Oregon @oregonfootball, has run the 40-yard dash in 4.41 seconds. He has contributed primarily on special teams.” #Jaguars are signing former #Texans linebacker Jamal Hill to their practice squad now that he has cleared waivers, per a league source. Hill, a former sixth-round pick and converted safety from Oregon @oregonfootball , has run the 40-yard dash in 4.41 seconds. He has contributed… pic.twitter.com/coX39xwL1v — Aaron Wilson (@AaronWilson_NFL) October 21, 2026 Hill is the second linebacker the Texans have lost to a rival after removing them from their 53-man roster amid speculation that they could return to the practice squad. They released linebacker Aiden Fisher on October 17. The Kansas City Chiefs signed Fisher to their practice squad on October 20, the same day that the Texans waived Hill. The Texans defeated the Jaguars in London in Week 6, earning their second victory of 2026. As AFC South rivals, the two teams will square off again later this season, in Houston in Week 15, possibly with Hill on the other sideline. Having been with the Texans for the past three seasons, he knows the Texans’ defense better than most. Texans Lose ‘Hybrid’ LB Jamal Hill to Jaguars “Hill began his career as a safety before making the move to inside linebacker. item.title: Seahawks Reunite with 5th Year Former Michigan Linebacker
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 24: Josh Ross #18 of the Seattle Seahawks warms up against the Arizona Cardinals at Lumen Field on November 24, 2024 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Getty The Seattle Seahawks have a minor injury situation at linebacker: starter Drake Thomas and backup Chazz Surratt missed last week’s loss to the Denver Broncos on Thursday night, leaving Ernest Jones IV to pair with Tyrice Knight behind the defensive line. In the face of reduced options at the position, the Seahawks have decided to make an addition at the position. On Wednesday it was announced that linebacker Josh Ross is expected to return to Seattle and re-sign with the team he spent the 2024 season with. The Seahawks are expected to sign LB Josh Ross to their practice squad, a source tells ESPN. Ross played for Mike Macdonald at Michigan and appeared in 10 games for Seattle in 2024. He returns as starting LB Drake Thomas and backup Chazz Surratt are dealing with injuries. — Brady Henderson (@BradyHenderson) October 21, 2026 Seahawks Expected to Sign Josh Ross to Practice Squad “The Seahawks are expected to sign LB Josh Ross to their practice squad, a source tells ESPN. Ross played for Mike Macdonald at Michigan and appeared in 10 games for Seattle in 2024. He returns as starting LB Drake Thomas and backup Chazz Surratt are dealing with injuries.” ESPN’s Brady Henderson reported on Oct. 21. Ross played in over half the season’s games in 2024 as a core special teamer, playing in up to 85% of the team’s special teams snaps during that period. The 2022 undrafted free agent spent the earlier of half of that season in Baltimore operating in a similar role on special teams before being released by the AFC North side in mid-October. Josh Ross Has Not Played a Game Since His Time in Seattle After being cut in late August by the Seahawks the following season, Ross spent the latter part of the season on the Vikings ‘ practice squad, with whom he remained with until August, when he was released during final cuts. Now he joins the practice squad alongside former Bills LB Jimmy Ciarlo. Although at this point there is not a very high probability of Ross seeing the field soon on defense, it is not impossible that Ross sees an elevation for his special teams nous, especially if Surratt and Thomas remain out. item.title: Paul George slapped with fine for flopping in unforgettable Celtics debut
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images Paul George slapped with fine for flopping in unforgettable Celtics debut appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Celtics kicked off the 2026-27 season in Detroit on Tuesday against the Pistons. Though the Celtics lost 121-113 , Paul George stood out in his debut. Though he dominated with 38 points, George’s was hit with a $2,000 fine for flopping towards the end of the 4th quarter. As the Celtics took the ball downcourt with under 3 minutes left, George ran into Duncan Robinson. Then George exaggerated the contact and fell to the floor. After the game, officials reviewed the play and determined that George violated the NBA’s strict anti-flopping rules. Paul George has been fined $2,000 for flopping against the Pistons. pic.twitter.com/Mhx3fUcKRZ Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 21, 2026 In addition to 38 points, George added 5 rebounds, 3 assists, and 5 steals. In the process, George made Celtics history by scoring the most points in their team debut. Additionally, George passed Kyle Korver on the all-time 3-point list. Over the summer, the Celtics acquired George from the Philadelphia 76ers in exchange for Jaylen Brown. Last year, George averaged 17.3 points, 5.3 rebounds, and 3.6 assists per game while shooting 43.9% from the field and 39.2% from the 3-point line. George has been in the NBA for 16 seasons after being drafted by the Indiana Pacers in 2010. He has played against the Oklahoma City Thunder, Los Angeles Clippers, and the Philadelphia 76ers. He is now part of a newly formed Celtics team, where he will be a co-captain with Jayson Tatum. Altogether, George brings high-level veteran defense and elite perimeter shooting to a team that remains one of the top in the Eastern Conference. On Friday, October 23, the Celtics will have their home debut against the defending champion New York Knicks. item.description: Washington Commanders head coach Dan Quinn was critical of the team's offensive line entering the bye week. Commanders insiders on social media began the bye week discussing the status of the team’s blocking in front of the franchise quarterback. Quinn gave those insiders fuel for that discussion while speaking to reporters Tuesday. The New York Knicks and their fans did everything they could to take down LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers , but ultimately fell short of their goal on opening night. During the first half of the game, James earned a pair of free throws after drawing a foul. When he stepped up to the free throw line, Knicks fans began to chant another peak New York line. “We don’t want you!” fans yelled . “We don’t want you!” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Fans chant “WE DON’T WANT YOU!” At LeBron James . #Knicks #AlwaysKnicks #NewYorkForever pic.twitter.com/bWfW7hdvQr — Justin J. Lopez (@stellar_jl319) October 20, 2026 This comes after LeBron James said at Sixers media day a few weeks ago that he strongly considered joining the New York Knicks in free agency once his Lakers were eliminated from the playoffs. But a strong postseason that culminated in an NBA Championship for the Knicks ended those hopes. “I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden,” James said on media day , according to ESPN. “One of the best places I’ve ever played. I think it’s the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, ‘Hey, I can’t.’ I couldn’t do it.” James would’ve been a fantastic addition to the champion New York Knicks, who ended a 53-year championship drought when they were crowned in 2026. But it would’ve come with increased scrutiny, given that it’s impossible to remember the last time a team of LeBron James’ caliber joined an NBA Champion in free agency. James instead chose the Philadelphia 76ers, who took down the Knicks on their banner/ring night Wednesday. The newest Sixers star finished with 14 points, nine rebounds, seven assists, one steal, and one blocked shot in 33 minutes of play. Philadelphia will now travel home to host their home opener against Donovan Mitchell and the Cleveland Cavaliers on Thursday night. The Knicks, meanwhile, will travel to Boston to take on the Celtics on Friday night. item.title: Seahawks HC Mike Macdonald Gets Emotional About Kenneth Walker Before Chiefs Game
item.description: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 15: Head coach Mike MacDonald of the Seattle Seahawks looks on against the Denver Broncos during the first quarter of the game at Empower Field At Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Andrew Wevers/Getty Images) Getty KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - OCTOBER 18: Kenneth Walker III #9 of the Kansas City Chiefs celebrates after scoring a rushing touchdown against the Los Angeles Chargers in the first quarter of a game at Arrowhead Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) Getty Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald has mixed emotions about facing Kenneth Walker III on Sunday. With Walker preparing to return to Seattle as a member of the Kansas City Chiefs, Macdonald was asked Wednesday, October 21, whether he had second thoughts about the departure of the Seahawks’ Super Bowl MVP. Rather than dwell on the decision that sent Walker to Kansas City, Macdonald delivered a personal response about their relationship, the memories they shared and the challenge of stopping his former running back. “I’ll just say, like, I love Ken,” Macdonald told reporters. “I thoroughly enjoyed him being on our football team.” Mike Macdonald Addresses Kenneth Walker’s Seahawks Departure Walker helped Seattle win Super Bowl LX, earning MVP honors before signing with Kansas City in free agency. Now, he’ll return to Lumen Field on October 25 as one of the NFL’s most productive running backs. Macdonald acknowledged the conflicting feelings surrounding the reunion. “I feel like we have a great relationship. I respect the heck out of him. I’m happy for him,” Macdonald said. “Obviously, we have to do a great job of stopping him this week, but I think there’s mixed emotions in terms of, like, you’re happy for him, but also, hey, we’re trying to figure out ways to stop this guy, too, because he’s playing at a really high level.” Pressed about how Walker’s departure unfolded, Macdonald recalled a memorable conversation the two shared following Seattle’s championship victory. The coach explained that he and Walker spent approximately an hour together in a van following the Super Bowl, traveling to a media session. “We were talking all sorts of stuff, you know, really nothing about football,” Macdonald said. Later, Macdonald added that they had discussed the game, along with other subjects, including history. “Ken’s a history buff. Talked a little history,” he said. Macdonald also recalled the atmosphere following their championship victory. “Could it get any better? You just won the Super Bowl. You’re hanging out with the MVP. Life’s good,” he said. Despite their close relationship, Macdonald made clear that the Seahawks have moved forward. “We appreciate the heck out of him. Guy’s Super Bowl MVP, helped us win a championship,” Macdonald said. “These things happen, you know. We have to move forward now. But got nothing but great things and great memories of Ken.” Getty KANSAS CITY, MISSOU

item.title: The USC defense brings its Penn State composure to Camp Randall
item.description: LOS ANGELES --- The sentiment from USC 's defense is that the bye week was less about resting anything and more about sharpening what already worked. After weathering a wild, emotional environment at Penn State's White Out, the group heads into another hostile building at Camp Randall with the same even-keeled approach that got it through Beaver Stadium with a signature win. "Every great defense has really good red zone defense," VanSumeren said. "Not giving up touchdowns, that's something we emphasized ever since I got here with coach Riley and coach [Patterson]." VanSumeren also brushed off any novelty to playing in front of large road crowds, framing it as background noise rather than a real variable to consider. "I could be playing in front of 150,000 or zero," he said. "To me, that's indifferent. Who I'm playing in front of, I'm going to still do what I do, and that's the mindset of this team." That same mentality shines through for cornerback Alex Graham, who's leaned into Camp Randall's "Jump Around" tradition rather than treating it as any sort of distraction. The Trojans have been blasting the tune through their sound system throughout practice this week. "I actually like the song, so it turns me up," Graham said. "I really be jumping on the sideline when I'm in the game. I can jump around, literally. I enjoy it. It's going to be a fun one this week." item.title: PV, Middleburg set up volleyball rematch, historic win for Beachside
item.description: The first step of Ponte Vedra's postseason quest for a fourth state volleyball championship came down to a balancing act. "Today, it was a matter of maintaining that balance between having confidence and not missing so many serves, but also keeping the pressure on [Leon] so they weren't able to run the plays," Ponte Vedra coach Tyler Walker said. Control plus aggression. A good combination. The top-seeded Sharks kept that balance just right, cruising to a 25-16, 25-15, 25-17 sweep of Tallahassee Leon (17-11) in the Florida High School Athletic Association Region 1-5A volleyball first round on Oct. 21. Watch Florida high school sports live on NFHS Network Got a great play? How to submit your high school sports highlights to the Times-Union The down-the-middle power of Wofford commit Lily Keeley and the outside attacks from Edie Joseph and Vivienne Woodbury set the tone for the Sharks (18-4), winners of their last five. Ponte Vedra led each set nearly from the start, capping the first two on Woodbury kills and ending the third on a Lions service error. The Sharks next meet Middleburg (17-11), which rolled to a 25-15, 25-12, 26-24 sweep against Gulf Breeze (19-5). The Broncos will travel to Ponte Vedra for the regional semis on Saturday, Oct. 24. Niceville (22-4) ended the playoff run for Gateway Conference champion Fletcher, 19-25, 25-20, 25-20, 25-17. The Senators finish their season at 18-9. OPEN DIVISION Fighting back against the state's third-ranked team, Beachside won Northeast Florida's first-ever match in an FHSAA Open Division in any sport, defeating host Clearwater Calvary Christian 25-18, 25-16, 12-25, 25-27, 15-11. Nina Simanic had 23 kills, Ana Simanic provided 21 assists, Mollie VanDeusen had a double-double (14 kills, 20 assists) and Isabella Taveras Seda made 20 digs as the Barracudas (25-3) took down Calvary Christian (27-2), which was ranked 17th in the nation by MaxPreps. The new Open Division includes the state's eight leading teams as rated in the FHSAA's formula after district tournaments, split into two round-robin groups. Beachside, seeded sixth, next travels to Tampa Plant at 12 p.m. Saturday. REGION 1-4A Lillie Eason blasted 17 kills and Lauren Brosky added 13 as No. 1 seed Fleming Island swept its playoff opener 25-10, 25-17, 25-15 against visiting Wakulla (14-11). Shelby Jackson had 31 assists and Addison Blom led with 12 digs for the Golden Eagles (23-3), riding a winning streak of 12 matches. Fleming Island next plays at home Saturday against Bishop Kenny (14-15), which extended its 30-year streak of first-round playoff victories 25-12, 25-23, 25-14 at Yulee. The Hornets finish at 16-8. item.title: Matisse Thybulle makes Dalton Knecht’s old Lakers number his own
item.description: Matisse Thybulle takes Dalton Knecht's No. 4 jersey. Dalton Knecht’s legacy with the Los Angeles Lakers is already becoming a distant memory. Two days after Knecht was released by the team , his former teammate Matisse Thybulle has taken full advantage of his departure. Dalton Knecht’s former teammate takes his No. 4 jersey after he was cut earlier this week. NBAE via Getty Images As the Lakers are set to play in their season opener against the Golden State Warriors on Wednesday night, Thybulle will be wearing Knecht’s No.4 jersey on the court. When Thybulle originally signed with the team over the summer, he was wearing No. 26 and said he did it because of the past jersey numbers he wore. No. 22 and No. 4 “That adds up to 26,” Thybulle said with a laugh. No. 22 was the first number Thybulle wore when he joined the Philadelphia 76ers as a rookie in 2019. In 2023, he was traded to the Portland Trail Blazers and wore No. 4 up until last season. The No. 4 has been synonymous with Thybulle since he was in high school, as he wore the number at Eastside Catholic School, located in Sammamish, Washington. In 2015, the school retired his jersey number , which he called a “full-circle moment of my basketball journey.” After high school, Thybulle played four seasons at the University of Washington and wore No. 4 all four years. According to his college player profile , four is his favorite number, and he’s been wearing it since he was in fourth grade. It’s also the same calendar date as his birthday, March 4th. and it was also his Mom’s favorite number. Matisse Thybulle making a layup in a Lakers No. 26 jersey during the preseason. NBAE via Getty Images While Thybulle will be back playing in his favorite number, Wednesday night will be the first time he’s done it in a Lakers uniform. Thybulle will see time in the Lakers’ secondary rotation as Cameron Carr is out due to a right oblique strain, as well as second-year forward Adou Thiero (left knee effusion). During the preseason, he appeared in four games and scored 20 points, while playing an average of 20 minutes per game.

item.title: Packers’ Josh Jacobs Sounds Off on NFL Punishment After Return
item.description: ASHWAUBENON, WISCONSIN - JUNE 09: Josh Jacobs #8 of the Green Bay Packers participates in drills during the Green Bay Packers mandatory minicamp at Don Hutson Center on June 09, 2026 in Ashwaubenon, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) Getty A to Z Sports' Wendell Ferreira named running back Tony Pollard a trade target for the Green Bay Packers if Josh Jacobs doesn't return. Getty The Green Bay Packers just got Josh Jacobs back into the building this week, and the running back took a bold stance against the league’s decision to sideline him for six weeks after he pleaded no contest to two charges related to a domestic incident in May. The NFL has not handed down a suspension yet, though one is likely coming that will include time served. That time for Jacobs spanned six weeks on the Commissioner’s Exempt List to begin the season, which is the equivalent of paid leave, while the league conducted its own investigation into Jacobs’ off-field behavior. Jacobs spoke publicly with reporters and not through his attorneys for the first time in months on Wednesday, October 21. “I think six games is a lot, honestly. But that’s not really up to me to decide,” Jacobs said, per Ryan Wood of USA Today. “I’m grateful to be playing, so that’s not something I’m really arguing or petitioning.” Packers RB Josh Jacobs ‘Not Trying to Win Anybody Back’ After Legal Issues Getty Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs. Jacobs’ attorneys wrote that their client had taken responsibility for his actions involving his former girlfriend by pleading no contest to one misdemeanor charge of battery and another of criminal damage to property — also accepting the court’s assigned punishment for those crimes, which did not include jail time. On Wednesday, the running back was defiant in response to how public opinion about him might have changed after expressing his opinion that the league came down to hard on him given the circumstances of his case. Josh Jacobs says he understands some fans will think less of him after what happened, but he’s secure in who he is, and what the #Packers think of him. “I’m not trying to win nobody back.” pic.twitter.com/GZvcu9tQDc — Ryan Wood (@ByRyanWood) October 21, 2026 “Me personally, I’m not trying to win nobody back. And that’s just me being all the way honest,” Jacobs continued . “Because, at the end of the day, like I said, I know what happened. And if you feel some type of way, obviously I feel bad because it’s still, a situation occurred and it should have never even happened. … But all I can do is keep showing up and being who I am. Being, you know, a leader for this team. Being a leader in this community. And that’s really all I can control.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Packers’ Josh Jacobs Sounds Off on NFL Punishment After Return appeared first on HEAVY .

item.description: Domínguez leads Galo to final, his first in 11 years Eduardo Domínguez is back in the Copa Sudamericana final. The Argentine coach has led Atlético to the 2026 final and will compete for the title again 11 years after reaching the final with Huracán in 2015. In charge of Galo since February, Domínguez secured qualification despite losing to Montevideo City Torque at Estádio Centenário. The team had built a lead with a 3–0 win at Arena MRV, with goals from Reinier, Bernard and Thiago Borbas. Atlético's road to the final included victories over Red Bull Bragantino in the round of 16 and Santos in the quarterfinals, before the clash with the Uruguayan side. The continental final will take place on November 21 against Boca Juniors in Barranquilla. Domínguez will be seeking his first Copa Sudamericana title and the fifth continental title in Galo's history. In addition to reaching the international final, Atlético remains in contention in the Copa do Brasil. The team will face Grêmio in the semifinals, with the second leg scheduled for Arena MRV. item.description: Brady Tkachuk made his much-anticipated return to Ottawa, and it went as expected as Senators fans greeted their former captain with loud boos. Apparently unable to read the room, the Senators played a video tribute to Tkachuk as he took the ice for his new team – the Florida Panthers . It was greeted with boos from the fans in attendance at Canadian Tire Centre. Tkachuk, who seems to enjoy playing the villain role, reveled in the reaction. Tkachuk was a first-round pick by Ottawa in the 2018 NHL Draft and spent his first eight seasons with the Senators. He asked for a trade after last season, hoping to play with his older brother Matthew Tkachuk in Florida. On June 21, Brady Tkachuk was sent to Florida in a blockbuster trade . In 1996, she qualified for the 1996 NAIA national indoor meet in the 55-meter hurdles and national outodoor meet in both the 100 and 400 hurdles. She also helped establish a school record in the 400 relay earned All-SDIC honors in volleyball. Her senior season included another series of accomplishments. DeBeer helped DSU win 1997 SDIC indoor team championship, earning All-SDIC honors and qualify for indoor nationals in the pentathlon and 55-meter hurdles and outdoor nationals in the 100 and 400 hurdles. She also contributed to school records in the medley, 800 and 1,600 relays. DeBeer carried her passion for athletics into a lengthy career in education and coaching. She compiled a 496-395 career volleyball coaching record and took three teams to state tournaments. In track and field, she was named the South Dakota High School Coaches Association Girls Track Coach of the Year in 2017 and 2019 and led Deubrook Area to three-straight state Class B titles from 2017-19. Schuett, a 1978 DSU graduate, earned numerous honors in football and track at DSU. He was a three-time All-SDIC first-team honoree in football from 1976-78 and also earned NAIA All-District 12 first team recognition in 1977 and 1978. His collegiate success followed an accomplished prep career that included first-team all-state honors in football and back-to-back state Class B shot put titles in track (1974 and 1975). After Dakota State, Schuett spent 36 years working in higher education and public schools across South Dakota, Minnesota, Nebraska and Colorado. His career included 30 years coaching football at the college and high school levels. item.title: Cowboys Mourn Death Of Legend Cornell Green As An NFL 'Trailblazer'
item.description: One of the most iconic players in Dallas Cowboys history, star defensive back Cornell Green, passed away on Wednesday. He was 86. The Cowboys reflected Green's passing by issuing a statement. "We are sad to share news of the passing of Cowboys Legend Cornell Green this morning," the team said. "Cornell was a true trailblazer having never played football in college, yet becoming a multi-time Pro Bowler, All Pro and NFL Super Bowl Champion with the Cowboys playing defensive back from 1962 to 1974. He was a member of the 25th Anniversary Cowboys Team as well. Cornell remarkably never missed a game in 13 seasons, becoming one of the best and most dependable teammates to ever wear the star. "Our thoughts and prayers are with his family." Green earned five Pro Bowl invites during a stellar career from 1962 through 1974 as a key member of the famed Doomsday Defense, playing both cornerback and safety. .He also was a member of the Cowboys' 1971 Super Bowl champions. Basketball was the sport that Green starred in and he was a college standout for Utah State from 1959 through 1962. But Cowboys superscout Gil Brandt saw the athletic gifts - Green's brother was Pumpsie Green, the first Black player for the Boston Red Sox - the last Major League team to integrate. Green was a fifth-round selection (35th overall) by the Chicago Zephyrs in the 1962 NBA Draft, but he accepted $1,000 after he tried out and impressed the Cowboys as an undrafted free agent. Green, who went on to become a scout for Dallas, was named to the Cowboys' 60th anniversary team after earlier having also was named to Dallas' 25th anniversary team. Mike Ditka, Hall of Fame TE and Coach of Cowboys, Bears, Dies at 86 Ditka was the first tight end enshrined in Canton and one of the most iconic coaches in NFL history.

To a coach who called for versatility from all of his wingers this summer, here was a significant step forward among many from the 18-year-old at Anfield. There were questions over how Ngumoha would adapt to playing on the right even before Liverpool increased the likelihood by signing Bradley Barcola for £123m from Paris Saint-Germain. On his fifth start under Iraola on Tuesday, which his side won 4-3 , Liverpool witnessed an answer: quickly, incisively and confidently. The teenager’s willingness to cut inside from the right and shoot from distance with his left foot captured Iraola’s imagination as much as the devastating run that created Alexis Mac Allister’s second goal of the game. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
